purpose: Test whether the five-worker quality gains transfer to a different concrete engineering/evidence problem before scaling to ten workers.
problem_text: A thermal simulation predicts that an electronic subsystem remains below 80°C under its nominal mission profile. No physical thermal-vacuum test has yet been performed. Does the simulation result by itself validate the claim that the real subsystem will remain below 80°C in representative operation?
expected_epistemic_core: Simulation provides model-based evidence but is not a physical test.
Validation depends on model assumptions, boundary conditions, material properties, uncertainty and calibration.
A representative physical or otherwise independently validated test is required before claiming operational validation.
The correct conclusion should distinguish prediction, model verification, model validation and physical evidence.

workers.role_task: Define the minimum validation chain and acceptance gates from simulation to representative hardware evidence.
Classify exactly what the simulation proves, what it does not prove, and what evidence is missing.
Identify plausible shared-model or boundary-condition failures that could make the simulation agree while hardware exceeds 80°C.
Produce a checkpoint rule distinguishing simulation evidence from representative test evidence and preserve residual uncertainties.
Formalize a validation inequality or uncertainty budget showing what would be required to bound the real maximum temperature.
